payload.label: Document Sections
payload.description: Place one named section into a markdown document, idempotently. The section identifies itself by its own first heading line: an existing section with that heading is replaced through to the next heading of the same or shallower depth, otherwise the section is appended. Headings inside fenced blocks never terminate a section. Publication is an atomic same-directory rename. This capability knows nothing about what any document is about; document path, section bytes and heading depth are all inputs.

payload.label: Document Sections
payload.description: Build the bytes of one markdown section out of a list of entries, so the result can be placed by the section-placing capability. Every line of an entry's text is emitted behind a blockquote marker and nothing else about it is changed, so the bytes between the markers are the bytes that came in; reformatting, trimming or collapsing would turn a record into a paraphrase that still looks like a record. A source naming no entry array, an entry missing its text field, and a set of sources holding nothing are all refused rather than rendered, because an empty section is indistinguishable from one that failed to find anything. This capability knows nothing about what any entry is about: the heading, the key the entries sit under, and the field names for text, label, timestamp and group are all inputs.
